description:
FILED s473t5a (#1501 CHECK 1 round 2, 2026-09-13).

TWO THINGS, one task because the first blocks the second.

(1) THE HANG.  `baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv` has
    op/gv.t   P 304/0   C 135/56   DIFF   aborted-forms:4: Died at gv.t line N.
Measured three times on this extraction (2026-09-13): TIMEOUT at 90 s with
C 67/24, the #366 serial re-run agreeing ("parallel TIMEOUT 67/24  serial
TIMEOUT 67/24  REAL MOVE"), and TIMEOUT again at **--timeout 400** with the
same 67/24.  A file that is merely slow finishes when the clock is raised;
this one does not, so it is a HANG at the same point, not the #326 clock.

IT IS NOT THIS ROUND'S CHANGE, measured two ways.  `./pl2cl < t/op/gv.t` on this tree and on a
`git archive 8c8fa4c0` extraction are BYTE-IDENTICAL (with both trees' root
paths normalised out of the preamble; `scratch/s473t5a/ab.sh` in the s473t5a
worktree), and nothing under `cl/` was touched, so the compiler output the run
executes is the same bytes either way.  The row is therefore NOT spliced.  And the BASE
EXTRACTION was run directly: `--jobs 1 --timeout 400` on the 8c8fa4c0 tree
gives the SAME `TIMEOUT 67/24`.

WHERE TO START: the file produces 91 rows and then stops.  `PCL_SUITE_KEEP=DIR`
keeps the four artifacts; the `.out` from the timed-out run ends inside SBCL's
compilation notes ("The variable &oonk is defined but never used"), i.e. the
TAP had not been flushed, so the row number where it stops must come from a
run that completes.  Bisect by line prefix with `tools/pclperl-for-tests`, or
run the kept `.lisp` under SBCL with the shadow t/ as CWD and a stack trace on
SIGQUIT.  Candidates worth eliminating first: the `DESTROY {eval {die …}}` at
gv.t:324 (global-destruction text), `local $SIG{__WARN__} = sub { die $_[0] }`
at 480, and the `sub STORE { die "No!" }` tie at 871 -- all three are
die-inside-a-handler shapes where a loop that re-enters the handler would spin.

(2) THE 113-ROW SHORTFALL, still UNEXPLAINED.  The snapshot's `sig` says four
top-level forms abort, each with perl's `Died at gv.t line N.` -- the message
`die` with no argument gives when `$@` is empty.  The file's candidate sites
are `die if $@;` at gv.t:346, 356, 360, `die if exists $::{BONK};` at 581 and
`… or die $@;` at 378, 434, 586 -- every one of them a glob/typeglob `eval`
whose failure the file turns into a die, so the four are FOUR separate glob
facts, not one cause.  Attributing them needs a completing run, i.e. (1) first.

SIZE: 113 rows of t/op/gv.t (and its 170 blessed fail rows / 126 clusters are
t5b's, `docs/plan-post-s473.md` section 5.4).  The shortfall row's cause names
this task.

=== s488a (2026-09-17, Opus, task #1834 member 2): WHEN IT STARTED, AND TWO
=== THINGS IT IS NOT ===

(A) THE COMMIT.  The hang begins at **0ea8d7e1** (s473h member 7, 2026-09-08,
"a BAREWORD ALONE AS A STATEMENT is perl's string constant, not a call",
#1249(7)).  Measured on `git archive` extractions, `--jobs 1`, the runner's own
serial re-run agreeing on each:
    a9f2a264 (s478)              op/gv.t DIFF 135/56   uni/gv.t DIFF 59/29
    e66761f4 (s473h member 4)    op/gv.t DIFF 135/56   uni/gv.t DIFF 59/29
    4f043b03, f492b7fc           DOCS ONLY (`git show --stat`: they file #1390
                                 and #1391, no code)
    0ea8d7e1 (s473h member 7)    op/gv.t TIMEOUT 67/24 uni/gv.t TIMEOUT 0/0
    6e0ce55d (s473h tip)         the same
`git rev-list --count e66761f4..0ea8d7e1` = 3 with the two middle commits
docs-only, so it is that ONE commit.  comp/use.t 42/45 -> 40/47 moves there too
(a different, understood effect of the same change).  This does NOT contradict
the "not this round's change" finding above: 0ea8d7e1 is five days BEFORE
8c8fa4c0, which is why the emission is byte-identical across that later pair.

WHAT 0ea8d7e1 CHANGES: `Pl/ExprToCL.pm` + `Pl/Parser2.pm` (a lone-bareword
statement lowers to `p-bareword-value` instead of `(pl-NAME)`), the runtime
gains `p-bareword-value`, generation v2-1080 -> v2-1120.  op/gv.t's own emitted
CL is byte-identical across it and so is perl-tests/t/test.pl's, and a WARM
cache re-run at 0ea8d7e1 hangs too, so the hang is in RUN-time behaviour that
the commit reaches some other way (a string eval's fragment, a child program,
or a module's emission -- not located).

(B) IT IS NOT THE `runperl` CHILD AT gv.t:321.  The last TAP row the kept `.out`
carries is 93, `__DIE__ handler never called` = t/op/gv.t:312, and the next
block (315-332) is the global-destruction `runperl(prog => ...)` #1651 named as
its first candidate.  Probed directly, both fast and clean:
    the child program alone, `./runpcl gv321.pl`   -> rc 0, no output, 0 s
      (perl prints "Farewell M=SCALAR(0x..)"; PCL does not run DESTROY at stash
       teardown, so the `like($output, qr/^Farewell/)` row fails -- an ordinary
       failing row, not a hang)
    the same program through a BACKTICK + tools/pclperl-for-tests, from inside
      a PCL program                                 -> 1 s, both children fine
So neither the child nor the runperl/backtick path hangs.

(C) THE `.out` CANNOT LOCATE IT ANYWAY -- filed as **#1850**.  perl's t/test.pl
sets `$| = 1` at its line 22 precisely so a test file's TAP reaches the disk row
by row.  PCL ignores `$|`: measured mid-run with the output redirected to a
file, perl has written 273 bytes where PCL has written 0, for a bare `print`,
for `print STDOUT` and for the classic `select((select(STDOUT), $|=1)[0])`
idiom alike; a 300-row (~9 KB) program still writes 0; and neither SIGTERM nor
SIGKILL flushes.  op/gv.t's kept `.out` holds 5,711 bytes of TAP (91 rows), so
at least one buffer was flushed and up to one more (~4 KB ~ 60 rows) was lost
with the kill.  READ THAT AS: the hang is at or AFTER gv.t:312, and the exact
row needs #1850 fixed first (or a run that completes, as this task already
said).  #1850 is the cheap unblock for this whole task.

WHAT THIS TASK STILL OWES: the run-time mechanism (start from what 0ea8d7e1
changes that op/gv.t's own emission does not contain -- its string evals and its
child programs are the two candidates) and then part (2), the four aborted
forms.  The snapshot row and the 113-row shortfall row now carry the commit.

=== s488a ADDENDUM, from the batch bar: THE HANG IS INTERMITTENT ===
The `--all --quick --jobs 2` companion of 2026-09-17 read op/gv.t as **DIFF 90/95**
in its PARALLEL pass -- 185 rows, and the verdict is DIFF, i.e. the file ENDED --
and TIMEOUT 67/24 in the #366 SERIAL re-run of the SAME run (the runner labelled
it `contention -- serial matches the snapshot` and recorded the serial).  So the
file is not an unconditional hang: it sometimes completes, getting 94 rows
further than the 91 the timed-out runs produce.  The 400 s run that still
TIMEOUTed at 67/24 (669 s wall) is therefore ONE SIDE OF A RACE, not a wall, and
the two clean child-process probes above are consistent with that.
WHAT TO DO WITH IT: a race that MORE load resolves points at something that
waits -- a child process, a pipe, or a lock -- rather than at an infinite loop in
emitted code.  Run the file alone in a loop (say 20 times, `--jobs 1`) and count
the two outcomes before looking anywhere else; #1850 first if the row where it
stops is wanted, since a killed run loses its last buffer.


=== CORRECTION to (C) (s489, Fable review) ===
PCL does NOT ignore `$|` (measured: `pcl FILE > out` writes 273 bytes mid-run
like perl; `./runpcl` shows 0 only because it captures stdout with backticks).
The kept `.out` IS still incomplete, for the reason #1850 now records: the
companion's shadow t/ loads PCL's stub perl-tests/t/test.pl, which lacks perl's
`$| = 1` at line 22, so the TAP is block-buffered and the kill drops up to one
buffer.  The reading stands -- the hang is at or after gv.t:312 -- and the
cheap unblock is the ONE-LINE stub fix in #1850 (harness bar), after which a
TIMEOUT run's `.out` ends at the hanging row.
subject: t/op/gv.t HANGS -- 400 s produces 67/24 of perl's 304 rows where the blessed snapshot says DIFF 135/56; the emission is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the snapshot's tree, so it is a RUN-time hang, and the 113-row shortfall's four aborted forms are still unattributed
